lines.rookie: Bitna, Haesu's daughter, was the last keeper. On 15 August 1945, Japan surrendered to the Allies and the war ended. Korea's light returned: gwangbok means the light comes back. The Allies won the war. Many Koreans, at home and far away, worked for this day too. Bitna's last note lies on top of Bun-i's first note.
lines.junior: Bitna, Haesu's daughter, was the last keeper. On 15 August 1945, Japan surrendered to the Allies, and the war came to an end. Korea's light returned: gwangbok means the light comes back. The Allies won the war, and many Koreans, at home and far away, also worked for this day. Bitna's last note rests on top of Bun-i's first note.
lines.master: Bitna, Haesu's daughter, was the final keeper. On 15 August 1945, Japan surrendered to the Allies and the war was over. Korea's light returned: gwangbok means the light comes back. The Allies won the war, yet many Koreans, both at home and far away, had also laboured for this day. Bitna's last note lies on top of Bun-i's first note.

lines.rookie:
The note says one word: 광복 (gwangbok).
"Gwang (광) is the opposite of dark."
"Bok (복) means it comes back."
"You have five tiles: H, T, I, G, L."
"Spell what gwang means, in English."
lines.junior:
The note has just one word: 광복 (gwangbok).
"Gwang (광) is the opposite of dark."
"Bok (복) means it comes back."
"You have five tiles: H, T, I, G, L."
"Spell out what gwang means, in English."
lines.master:
The note holds a single word: 광복 (gwangbok).
"Gwang (광) is the opposite of dark."
"Bok (복) means that it comes back."
"You have five tiles: H, T, I, G, L."
"Spell, in English, what gwang means."

lines.rookie: Spell the word with your five tiles.
lines.junior: Use your five tiles to spell the word.
lines.master: Arrange your five tiles to spell the word.

lines.rookie: Gwang is the opposite of dark.
lines.junior: Gwang means the opposite of dark.
lines.master: Gwang stands for the opposite of dark.

lines.rookie: Day is full of it; night has very little.
lines.junior: The day has lots of it; the night has very little.
lines.master: Daytime overflows with it; night holds precious little.

lines.rookie: LIGHT. The light returns!
lines.junior: LIGHT. The light returns!
lines.master: LIGHT. The light returns!

lines.rookie: Bitna lays her note on top of the others.
lines.junior: Bitna places her note on top of the others.
lines.master: Bitna lays her note upon the others.

lines.rookie: Bun-i's first note lies under eleven more.
lines.junior: Now eleven notes lie on top of Bun-i's first note.
lines.master: Bun-i's first note now rests beneath eleven more.

lines.rookie: The box is full of light now. The season ends.
lines.junior: Now the box is full of light. The season is over.
lines.master: The box is filled with light at last. The season draws to a close.

lines.rookie: All five tiles are right. What is the opposite of dark?
lines.junior: All five tiles are correct. What is the opposite of dark?
lines.master: Each of the five tiles is correct. What is the opposite of dark?

lines.rookie: THE KEEPERS' LAST LOCK
lines.junior: THE KEEPERS' LAST LOCK
lines.master: THE KEEPERS' LAST LOCK

lines.rookie: On 15 August 1945, Japan surrendered to the Allies.
lines.junior: On 15 August 1945, Japan surrendered to the Allies.
lines.master: On 15 August 1945, Japan surrendered to the Allies.

lines.rookie: The war ended, and Korea's light returned: gwangbok.
lines.junior: The war came to an end, and Korea's light returned: gwangbok.
lines.master: The war was over, and Korea's light had returned: gwangbok.

lines.rookie: Kim Won-bong had worked for independence since 1919.
lines.junior: Kim Won-bong had been working for independence since 1919.
lines.master: Kim Won-bong had laboured for independence ever since 1919.

lines.rookie: No one person brought this day.
lines.junior: This day was not brought by just one person.
lines.master: No single person brought about this day.

lines.rookie: The Allies won the war, and many Koreans worked for it.
lines.junior: The Allies won the war, and many Koreans worked for it too.
lines.master: The Allies won the war, while many Koreans laboured for it as well.

lines.rookie: At home and far away. Most of their names are unknown.
lines.junior: Both at home and far away. Most of their names are not known.
lines.master: At home and in distant lands. Most of their names remain unknown.

lines.rookie: Bun-i's first note started it all.
lines.junior: It all began with Bun-i's first note.
lines.master: It all began with Bun-i's very first note.

lines.rookie: Gwangbok. The light returns.
lines.junior: Gwangbok. The light returns.
lines.master: Gwangbok. The light returns.
